concepts.title: Data
concepts.definition: Numbers, measurements or observations gathered about the things we want to study -- gathered together, they are called data.
concepts.key_idea: Information collected to convey facts or observations.
question_patterns: what is data
define data
give examples of data
identify if a collection of facts is data
Give one example of data from your classroom.
Why organise raw observations before drawing conclusions?

solution_steps.explain: Check if the information consists of facts, numbers, or observations.
Determine whether the data is numerical (counts or measurements) or categorical (labels or categories).
Conclude that the collection is data if it was gathered purposefully to convey facts about the things being studied.

concepts.title: Tally Marks and Frequency
concepts.definition: Tally marks record counts in little bundles of five -- four strokes plus one strike across. A frequency is simply how often a particular value shows up.
concepts.key_idea: Bundle strokes in fives, then read each row's count as its frequency.
question_patterns: prepare a frequency distribution table
how many students chose a specific category using tallies
find the frequency of a value
complete the tally mark table
Draw the tally for a count of 12.
What does a strike across four strokes stand for?

solution_steps.explain: Each group of four marks with a diagonal line represents 5 units.
Add the individual vertical lines to the group count.
Write the total count beside the tally row in the frequency column of the distribution table.

concepts.title: Pictographs
concepts.definition: A picture chart where each drawn symbol stands for a fixed number of things, so a reader can take in the figures at a glance.
concepts.key_idea: Using visual symbols and a scale to represent numerical data.
question_patterns: how many items are represented in the pictograph
calculate the total from the pictograph
find the value for a category in a pictograph
how many symbols represent a specific number
If one symbol stands for 5 books, how many symbols show 35 books?
Read the grand total from the given picture chart.

solution_steps.explain: Determine how many units one symbol represents.
Count the number of complete symbols for the category.
If a half symbol is present, add half of the scale value.

concepts.title: Bar Graphs
concepts.definition: A chart of equally spaced, same-width bars whose heights (or lengths) carry each category's count.
concepts.key_idea: Visual comparison of frequencies using rectangular bars.
question_patterns: interpret the bar graph
find the value of a category from the bar graph
which category has the maximum frequency
calculate the difference between two bars
Which bar is tallest and what does that tell you?
By how much do the two tallest bars differ?

solution_steps.explain: Identify the height or length of the bar on the axis.
Multiply the units by the scale factor defined for the axis.
To find a difference or maximum, repeat the reading for each relevant bar and subtract or compare the values.

concepts.title: Drawing a Bar Graph (Scale Selection)
concepts.definition: Pick how many units one step of the axis should carry so the tallest value still fits on the sheet -- that choice is the scale.
concepts.key_idea: Determining the physical height of bars based on frequency and chosen scale.
question_patterns: calculate the height of the bar
what scale should be used for the bar graph
how many units represent the frequency
determine the number of units for a specific expenditure
Choose a scale so values up to 200 fit in 20 divisions.
What drawn height does a frequency of 24 take at 1 unit = 4?

solution_steps.explain: Determine the data value and the chosen unit scale.
Divide the frequency by the scale to find the number of units to draw.

solution_steps.action: verify the bar fits the sheet
solution_steps.explain: Check that the computed height does not exceed the available axis divisions; if it does, choose a larger scale and recompute.

concepts.title: Column Graphs and Horizontal Bars
concepts.definition: Bars can stand upright or lie flat; upright suits heights, flat suits lengths measured along the ground.
concepts.key_idea: Orientation of bars based on the nature of the data (height vs distance).
question_patterns: what is a column graph
when to use vertical bars
when to use horizontal bars
identify the best graph orientation for heights
Should bars for river lengths stand upright or lie flat?
When are flat bars easier to label?

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the data represents vertical measures (heights) or horizontal measures (distances).
Select vertical (column) bars for heights and horizontal bars for distances or long category labels.
Verify that the chosen orientation makes the graph easy to label and compare without crowding the axis.

concepts.title: Infographics
concepts.definition: Posters that blend charts, icons and short text into one striking visual -- eye-catching, but distorted shapes can mislead.
concepts.key_idea: Engaging visual communication of data, with a warning about potential misleading shapes.
question_patterns: define infographics
what is the purpose of an infographic
can infographics be misleading
how do infographics differ from standard bar graphs
Why can an infographic exaggerate a comparison?
What should you check before trusting a poster's visual?

solution_steps.explain: Check if artistic shapes (like triangles) maintain proportional accuracy to the data.

solution_steps.action: compare with a standard bar graph
solution_steps.explain: Contrast the infographic's visual encoding against an equivalent bar graph to spot any exaggeration or distortion.
Conclude whether the infographic conveys the data faithfully or misleads the reader through scaled icons or decorative effects.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How many children sometimes slept at least 9 hours if there are {count} complete pictures and {partial} half picture where one symbol is {scale} children?

solution_template.explain: Multiply the number of full symbols by the scale.
A half symbol represents half of the scale.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Calculate the height of the bar for {item} with expenditure {exp} if 1 unit length = {scale} rupees.

solution_template.explain: The height in units is the total value divided by the value per unit.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Bundle {n} strokes and read the frequency.
A row shows one crossed bundle plus {k} singles -- what is the frequency?
One symbol equals {scale} books; how many books do {symbols} symbols show?
Each cart icon means {scale} sacks; read the total for {symbols} icons.
A bar reaches {bars} units at a scale of {scale} per unit -- what value shows?
Two bars measure {b1} and {b2} units at {scale} per unit -- find the gap.
At 1 unit = {scale}, what height does a frequency of {frequency} take?
Fit {frequency} into 10 divisions, then read the drawn height.
